messages:
incident-bot: P1 Alert: TENANT 'Haven' — partial egress failures from eu-west1 to 3rd-party integrations. Automated detection: 50% request errors (502/504) to external auth from tenant-dedicated pools. Paging on-call stack now.

sre-amy: on it. pulling logs and checking pool dp-haven-01.

oncall-eng: seeing higher tail latency on dp-haven-01, some pods show repeated connection resets to auth gateway.

infra-ben: FYI we've got scheduled maintenance on the auth gateway in eu-west1 that started around the same time — looks like it retried to old endpoint. I'm confirming config.

network-jordan: checked networking — VPC peering to partner-auth has intermittent flaps from eu-west1b -> eu-west1c. BGP flaps detected. Routing team alerted.

cs-luke: Maria (Haven SRE) on the line, customers reporting management console 503s and some inference requests failing. Maria will coordinate on customer-side DNS if needed.

customer-sre-maria: Confirmed — live traffic to our tenant shows ~40% 5xx to external auth; we're throttling retries per our side but want Redwood to isolate tenant traffic ASAP. We can cutover to backup auth endpoint if you coordinate.

sre-amy: mitigation plan: 1) isolate Haven to warm fallback pool in eu-west2 (reserved warm capacity, dp-haven-warm-02) 2) shift majority of traffic to eu-west2 via weighted DNS at Atlas-DNS 3) reduce TTL and perform phased CNAME weight steps 4) if healthy, promote eu-west2 as primary until routefix.

infra-ben: warming dp-haven-warm-02 now. Snapshot restore in progress (ETA ~6m). I'll keep logs here: `restore job 0x7f3d`

network-jordan: I'll hold DNS change window. Need CS approval for customer-facing cutover. Maria, do you want us to modify your tenant CNAME or do you want to update on your side?

customer-sre-maria: We prefer Redwood to do a weighted DNS shift for now. We'll update auth failover config to accept eu-west2 callbacks. Confirm once done and we'll lift throttles.

eng-frontend: quick note — reduced retry loops in frontend SDK have been pushed to canary. Should reduce amplification if cutover goes flaky.

cs-luke: Approved. Proceed with weighted shift. I'll message Haven support channel.

incident-bot: Action assigned -> sso:make-weighted-dns-change to network-jordan (priority high).

network-jordan: Changing TTL to 60s on `haven.api.redwood.example` at Atlas-DNS. Then shifting weights: eu-west1:20% -> eu-west2:80% in 3 steps. Executing step 1 now.

sre-amy: health checks running against dp-haven-warm-02. Initial API probe OK (200, avg 45ms). Authentication handshake looks healthy.

network-jordan: Step 1 applied: eu-west2=50% eu-west1=50%

customer-sre-maria: seeing reduction in 5xx from our side, trending down to ~12%. Good so far.

infra-ben: dp-haven-warm-02 restored and joined service mesh. KV cache primed via prefix-sync.

network-jordan: Step 2 applied: eu-west2=75% eu-west1=25%

sre-amy: monitoring error budget and latency. Rolling health summary: requests from haven -> external auth through eu-west2 show success 99.2% over 2m window. No retry storms.

eng-frontend: no alerts from frontend canary. SDK retries stable.

network-jordan: Step 3 applied: eu-west2=95% eu-west1=5%

customer-sre-maria: Haven console errors down to single digits. We're re-enabling some background jobs. Thanks.

sre-amy: next steps: keep weighted shift for 30m, then decide if we failover DNS fully or revert when partner BGP is stable. Also plan to evacuate other tenants away from the affected auth gateway to reduce cross-impact.

cs-luke: I'll send a customer update: we've isolated traffic and shifted most traffic to warm pool in eu-west2; ps. ETA for full resolution depends on partner network fix.

incident-bot: Note added to incident timeline by cs-luke.

network-jordan: Routing team reports partner fixed BGP abnormalities on peer-auth, monitoring for 5m of stability.

sre-amy: health checks remain green. Recommend full DNS failover only if partner confirms sustained stability or we prefer to keep haven in eu-west2 until maintenance window. Maria, what do you prefer?

customer-sre-maria: We'll accept staying in eu-west2 for now — want to avoid flip-flopping while heaviest daily traffic is still active. We'll coordinate a planned migration back during our next low-traffic window.

infra-ben: locking dp-haven-warm-02 in production config and promoting monitoring retention. I'll also isolate the auth gateway instance for postmortem trace capture.

oncall-eng: Handoff note: I'm oncall until +45m. sre-amy take over after that. Leaving checklist: keep TTL=60s, keep weights at eu-west2=95%, watch 5xx <1% and latency p95 < 250ms.

sre-amy: acked. I'll take post-handoff. Starting incident postmortem draft: root cause likely partner BGP flap -> auth endpoint instability -> time-of-day correlation with partner deploy.

cs-luke: Customer comms sent: "We've isolated your tenant to a nearby warm pool and reduced failed requests. No data lost; authentication retries were rate-limited. Working with your SRE on next steps."

incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated (customer traffic shifted). Keep monitoring; update incident when moved to resolved.

customer-sre-maria: Thanks everyone. We'll schedule joint RCA with partner and Redwood tomorrow.

sre-amy: adding action items: (1) formalize auto-weighted fallback play for dedicated tenants, (2) page routing team to add partner to BGP monitoring, (3) update runbook with dp-haven-warm snapshot steps.

infra-ben: noted and creating infra ticket INF-4981 for warm pool automation improvements.

oncall-eng: closing real-time ops loop. Leave any follow-ups in #incidents-postmortems. :white_check_mark:
